title: Matters, contacts, firm home and search
summary: The matter is the system of record for the firm. The agent keeps a cited matter brief, plans the stages, and proposes contacts and roles drawn from email and documents. Humans approve anything that changes conflict data, key facts or client-facing state. Contacts and their roles feed the conflict check, so merges, role changes and new adverse parties all pass a gate.

screens.name: Firm home
screens.purpose: Each person's daily starting point: approvals waiting, deadlines and matters at risk.
screens.layout: Top: approval inbox counts by gate. Left: my matters with a status digest. Right: deadlines over the next 14 days, and trust and AR alerts. Bottom: agent activity feed.

fields.name: approvals_waiting
fields.note: Grouped by G-id. Each count links to its queue.

fields.name: my_matters
fields.note: Responsible or assigned. Sorted by risk score.

fields.name: upcoming_deadlines
fields.note: Only confirmed deadlines count as authoritative. Unconfirmed ones carry a separate badge.

fields.name: stale_matters

fields.name: unbilled_wip
fields.note: Per user, or firm-wide for admins.

fields.name: trust_alerts
fields.note: Low retainer, or a client ledger near zero. Lawyers and admins only.

fields.name: agent_feed
fields.note: What the agent did since the user last logged in.

fields.name: my_time_today
fields.note: Hours recorded today against the user's daily target, from the time module.

fields.name: followed_matters
fields.note: Recent changes on matters the user follows.

actions.note: Opens the filtered approvals inbox.

actions.name: Ask the firm
actions.note: Plain-language question. The answer cites matter records and respects ethical walls.

actions.name: Snooze stale flag
actions.note: Snoozes for a set period. The reason is logged.

actions.name: Compose morning digest
actions.note: Internal only.

actions.name: Rearrange or hide cards
actions.note: Per-user layout.

screens.agent: Before the workday starts, the agent builds each person's digest. It ranks matters by risk (unconfirmed deadline, limitation within 90 days, no activity, retainer below threshold, unsigned engagement letter) and proposes one next action per matter.
screens.gate: none (the screen only views and routes; each linked approval keeps its own gate)
edge: The user is behind an ethical wall: walled matters must not appear in any count or feed item.
A deadline has no confirmation: show it as provisional and never in green.
A large firm has many approvals: paginate per gate and never truncate silently.
screens.reg: Supervision of non-lawyers and of agent work (RPC 6.1, verify). A limitation date shown as confirmed must have passed gate G7 (Limitations Act, 2002).

screens.name: Matter list
screens.purpose: Find, filter and triage every matter the user is allowed to see.
screens.layout: Saved views on the left (Mine, Open, By stage, Closing). Filter bar plus a table in the centre. The row drawer on the right shows the agent's digest. A toggle switches the table to the stage board.

fields.name: short_name

fields.name: trust_balance
fields.note: Hidden for roles without trust access.

fields.name: status_tab
fields.note: Quick tabs: open | pending | closed | all. Pending means accepted but not yet opened, or winding down (the firm picks which in settings).

fields.name: columns
fields.note: Column picker per user, including any custom field; stored with the saved view.

fields.name: tags
fields.note: Free labels on matters (e.g. 'legal aid', 'rush'); filterable.

fields.name: client_reference
fields.note: The client's own file or claim number; searchable.

fields.name: following
fields.note: Matters the user follows get change notifications even when not on the team.

fields.name: responsible_staff
fields.note: Available in the column picker and as a filter.

actions.name: Filter, sort and save a view
Open a new matter
actions.note: Opens the matter-opening wizard.

actions.name: Bulk change responsible lawyer
actions.note: A lawyer or admin approves. Logged per matter.

actions.name: Bulk change status or stage
actions.note: Never available for closing; closing goes through the closing area (G13).

actions.name: Export CSV
actions.note: Respects walls. The export is audit-logged.

actions.name: Propose next actions
actions.note: Suggestions only; they show in the drawer.

actions.name: Bulk set a custom field value
actions.note: Same G-BK gate; preview lists every matter and old value first.

actions.name: Bulk add or remove tags
actions.note: Tags carry no conflict or client-facing effect.

actions.name: Bulk close
actions.note: Does not close directly: opens the closing checklist (platform matter-closing) for each selected matter.

actions.name: Print or PDF the current view
actions.note: Watermarked with user and time.

screens.agent: The agent keeps agent_flag and a one-line digest current for each matter, recomputed on every event. It proposes one next action per row (for example, 'draft the statement of claim; limitation 2026-11-20').
screens.gate: Bulk changes to responsible lawyer, status or stage need lawyer or admin approval before they apply.
edge: A walled matter must not leak through counts, autocomplete or export.
Matter number collision on import: reject and keep the legacy number in a separate field.
A matter with no responsible lawyer is invalid and shows as blocked.
Bulk change spans matters the user cannot see behind a wall: those are silently excluded and the preview counts them as 'not permitted'.
A bulk custom-field set where the field is not in a matter's practice-area set: skipped with a reason rather than adding the field.
Saved view references a deleted custom field: column drops out and the view owner is told.
screens.reg: Confidentiality and ethical walls (RPC 3.3 and 3.4, verify). Exports are audit-logged.

screens.name: Matter stage board
screens.purpose: Shows the matters in one practice area by stage and lets users move them along.
screens.layout: One column per stage for the selected practice area. Each card shows the matter, the lawyer, days in stage and blockers. A side panel lists the matters the agent proposes to advance, with the evidence for each.

fields.name: practice_area
fields.note: Each area has its own stage set.

fields.name: entry_criteria_met
fields.note: Evidence-based, e.g. signed engagement letter present.

actions.name: Drag a card to another stage
actions.note: Moves to a stage flagged 'client-facing' or 'billing' require approval.

actions.name: Propose stage advance
actions.note: The proposal cites evidence, such as a filed document or a paid bill.

screens.agent: The agent watches for evidence events (document filed, letter signed, bill paid, deadline passed) and proposes stage moves with links to that evidence. It flags any matter that has been in one stage longer than the area's expected duration.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves any move into a stage that triggers a client-facing message, a bill or the closing workflow.
edge: A matter changes practice area: map its stage to the new area or reset it, and log the old stage.
Two users move the same card at once: the last write is rejected and the user sees the current stage.
A stage is deleted while matters sit in it: the delete is blocked until they move.

screens.name: Open a matter
screens.purpose: Turns an accepted, conflict-cleared intake into an open matter with parties, fields, a stage and a task plan.
screens.layout: Five steps across the top: 1 Client & source, 2 Parties & roles, 3 Practice area & custom fields, 4 Team, billing & stage, 5 Review. The agent's pre-fill is shown with a source chip on each field.

fields.name: source_intake
fields.note: When set, the agent pre-fills from the intake summary.

fields.name: client
fields.note: Existing contact or a new one. A duplicate check runs.

fields.name: parties
fields.note: At least the client. Adverse parties are required for litigation areas.

fields.name: conflict_check
fields.note: Must be in state cleared or consent-on-file (G2).

fields.name: client_id_status
fields.note: Pending is allowed to open, but blocks trust receipts until G4.

fields.name: engagement
fields.note: Signed (G5), or a recorded exception approved by a lawyer.

fields.name: custom_fields
fields.note: From the practice area's field set. Its required flags apply.

fields.name: responsible_lawyer
fields.note: Must be a licensee.

fields.name: ethical_wall
fields.note: Users to exclude from the matter.

fields.name: responsible_staff
fields.note: Clerk or paralegal who runs the file day to day, beside the responsible and originating lawyer. The agent routes clerk-level work items to this person by default.

actions.name: Re-run conflict on new parties
actions.note: Adding a party not in the original check re-opens G2.

actions.name: Open matter
actions.note: The responsible lawyer confirms. The matter number is assigned at this point.

actions.name: Create folders, task plan and calendar placeholders
actions.note: Runs after opening. Deadlines are created as unconfirmed (G7).

screens.agent: The agent pre-fills every step from the intake, conflict memo and engagement letter, and attaches a source to each value. It suggests the practice area and the custom-field values, drafts the description, and proposes the team and the task plan. It refuses to submit if G2 or G5 is not satisfied.
screens.gate: The responsible lawyer approves the opening. That approval confirms the parties, the practice area and the billing method. Any party added after the conflict check triggers a fresh G2 sign-off.
edge: The client is an organization with no ID record: the matter can open, but the trust panel shows a G4 block.
Urgent matter (limitation within days): an approved exception lets it open before the engagement letter is signed, and it is logged.
Joint clients: a joint-retainer disclosure must be recorded (RPC 3.4, verify).
The intake is abandoned midway: the draft expires after 30 days, and conflict-relevant data is kept under the prospective-client rule.
screens.reg: Conflicts (RPC 3.4) must clear before opening. Client identification under By-Law 7.1 is required at opening; verification is required before funds move (verify). The fee agreement must comply with RPC 3.6 and the Solicitors Act. Contingency terms are subject to O. Reg. 563/20 (verify).

screens.name: Matter overview
screens.purpose: Shows the state of one matter on a single page: the brief, the parties, what is due and the money position.
screens.layout: Header with number, name, status, stage, lawyer and a wall badge. Tabs: Overview, Parties, Notes, Activity, Financial, plus links to other areas (Docs, Calendar, Tasks, Bills). Overview has the agent brief on the left; key fields, next deadlines and open approvals on the right.

fields.name: brief
fields.note: Agent-maintained. Each statement links to a document, email or note.

fields.name: key_facts
fields.note: Examples: incident date, property address, court file no. Edits are gated.

fields.name: limitation_date
fields.note: Confirmed via G7 only.

fields.name: open_items
fields.note: Tasks, approvals and unconfirmed deadlines.

fields.name: status
fields.note: open | pending | closed; each change stamps its own date.

fields.name: close_date
fields.note: Set only by the closing flow.

fields.name: related_matters
fields.note: Link to other matters with a reason: same client, same transaction, appeal of, related claim. Feeds conflict context.

fields.name: followers
fields.note: Users notified of changes without being on the team.

fields.name: matter_location
fields.note: Office or region handling the file, for multi-office firms.

fields.name: responsible_staff
fields.note: Shown in the header next to the responsible lawyer. Change is logged, no gate.

actions.name: Ask about this matter
actions.note: Opens matter-ask. The answer cites sources inside this matter only, to page and line.

actions.name: Edit key fact
actions.note: A change to a party, a key date or the court file no. is logged with the old value.

actions.name: Propose key-fact change
actions.note: Raised when new evidence contradicts a stored fact.

actions.name: Link related matter
actions.note: Agent may propose links (same parties, same property) for confirmation.

actions.name: Change status to pending
actions.note: Lawyer approves; pending stops new time entry by default.

actions.name: Reopen closed matter
actions.note: Routes to platform matter-closing 'Reopen'; reason required.

actions.name: Apply template to this matter
actions.note: Shows a preview of what the template would add (fields, folders, work items, billing preset). Nothing already set is overwritten unless the user ticks it. The responsible lawyer approves (G-AT).

actions.name: Suggest a template
actions.note: When a matter has no template, the agent proposes the best fit from the practice area and past matters, with its reasons.

actions.name: Open chronology
actions.note: Opens matter-chronology.

screens.agent: The agent rewrites the brief after each new document, email, note or event, citing every claim. It detects contradictions between a new document and the stored key facts (for example, a different incident date) and raises a change proposal instead of editing the fact.
screens.gate: The responsible lawyer approves changes to key facts, parties or the responsible lawyer. Reading needs no approval.
edge: Brief claim without a source: it is not shown.
A user behind the wall opens a direct URL: return 404, not 403, so the matter's existence does not leak.
A closed matter receives new mail: the agent flags it to the lawyer and does not reopen the matter.
Related matter is walled from this user: link shows as 'restricted matter' with no name.
Status set to closed by import while trust balance is non-zero: import refuses that row.
Template applied to a matter whose practice area differs from the template's: refuse, and offer the templates for the matter's area.
Template adds a required custom field the matter lacks: the field is added empty and listed as an open item; the matter is not blocked.
screens.reg: Accuracy of the record and privilege. Walls (RPC 3.4, verify).

screens.name: Matter parties and roles
screens.purpose: Lists everyone connected to the matter and their role in it, including opposing counsel and related parties.
screens.layout: Table grouped by side (Our client, Adverse, Neutral, Court/Other). A proposals strip at the top lists parties the agent found in documents or email.

fields.name: represented_by
fields.note: Links an adverse party to their counsel.

fields.name: conflict_relevant
fields.note: Derived from the role. Adverse, co-client and related parties are true.

fields.name: end_date
fields.note: A role is ended, never deleted, so conflict history survives.

fields.name: lso_number
fields.note: For opposing counsel or paralegal (optional, for reference).

fields.name: bill_recipient
fields.note: Who receives bills for this matter; more than one allowed with split percentages (billing area owns the split).

fields.name: relationship_label
fields.note: Free text beyond the role, e.g. 'adjuster for defendant's insurer'.

actions.name: Add party
actions.note: A conflict-relevant role runs a conflict check and needs G2 sign-off before it becomes active.

actions.name: Propose party from document or email
Mark opposing counsel as representing a party
actions.note: Once set, it routes the no-contact warning: do not message a represented party directly.

screens.agent: The agent extracts names, organizations and counsel from pleadings, correspondence and closing documents, and matches them to existing contacts. It proposes roles and starts the conflict check on any new conflict-relevant party.
screens.gate: A new conflict-relevant party (adverse, co-client or related company) becomes active only after a lawyer signs off its conflict check (G2). Ending a role needs approval.
edge: The same contact appears on both sides: blocked, with the result shown as a conflict.
Opposing counsel changes firms: end the old role and add the new one, keeping history.
A party is a minor or a person under disability: a litigation guardian role is required (verify the RCP rule).
An adverse party is a related company of a current client: the check must surface the corporate relationship.
Removing the only bill recipient: blocked until another is chosen.
Same contact holds two roles on one matter (client and guarantor): allowed, both shown, both sent to conflict index.
screens.reg: RPC 3.4 (conflicts, including related entities). RPC 7.2 on communicating with a represented person (verify). Role history is kept for future conflict checks.

screens.name: Matter notes and activity
screens.purpose: A single timeline of everything that happened on the matter (human and agent), with notes alongside.
screens.layout: Filter chips (notes, emails, calls, documents, events, approvals, agent actions, stage changes). Reverse-chronological timeline. A note composer at the top.

fields.name: body
fields.note: Notes only. Stored in the firm cell, not in platform metadata.

fields.name: note_date
fields.note: Defaults today; may be backdated with the real entry time kept in the audit.

fields.name: note_target
fields.note: matter | contact. Contact notes show on every matter where that contact is a party, if permitted.

actions.name: Draft call summary note
actions.note: The participant confirms it is accurate before it enters the record.

actions.name: Propose time entry from activity
actions.note: Goes to the G9 queue.

actions.name: Edit note
actions.note: Versioned. The original is kept.

actions.name: Create time entry from note
actions.note: Pre-fills duration and narrative; time module owns approval.

actions.name: Filter timeline by type, actor, date
Export timeline as PDF
actions.note: Lawyer approves because the export can include privileged entries.

screens.agent: The agent writes an activity entry for every action it takes, saying what it did, why, and from which inputs. It summarises calls and meetings into draft notes and pulls out commitments as tasks.
screens.gate: A person confirms each agent-drafted note or call summary before it becomes part of the record. Activity entries cannot be edited.
edge: Note deleted: it is soft-deleted, with an audit entry kept.
Call recorded without consent recorded: the summary is blocked.
Very long timeline: paged, with a jump-to-date control.
Backdated note: displays its stated date but sorts with a 'entered later' marker.
Private task or private note: excluded from the timeline for everyone but creator, assignee and admins.
screens.reg: Notes may become evidence and must be preserved. Consent is required to record calls (verify for Canada and Ontario). Privilege marking applies.

Note: client confirmed two witnesses, names to follow
Stage proposal: Intake complete -> Pleadings (evidence: signed engagement letter)

screens.name: Matter financial summary
screens.purpose: Shows the money position of one matter at a glance (read-only here) and links to billing and trust.
screens.layout: Tiles: Unbilled time, Unbilled disbursements, Outstanding AR, Trust balance, Budget used. Below: recent bills and recent trust transactions, with links to the billing and trust areas.

fields.name: trust_balance
fields.note: Taken from the client trust ledger and never computed here.

actions.name: Request retainer top-up
actions.note: Drafts the trust request. A lawyer approves before it is sent.

actions.name: Start bill draft
actions.note: Hands off to the billing area (G-B2).

screens.agent: The agent watches trust against the retainer floor and budget against estimate. When either crosses its threshold, it drafts a top-up request or a budget update for the client.
screens.gate: No money moves from this screen. Client-facing requests (top-up, budget update) need lawyer approval.
edge: Trust is negative on the ledger: show it as a critical BL9 exception and escalate. This should never happen.
Contingency matter: show disbursements and the accrued fee estimate, not hourly WIP.
The viewer's rates.view capability is 'own' or 'none': other timekeepers' rates are hidden on this screen and in its export; totals still show.
screens.reg: BL9: per-client trust ledger, no overdrawn client balances (verify). HST on fees and disbursements.

screens.name: Contacts
screens.purpose: Directory of people and organizations, with duplicate review.
screens.layout: Tabs: People, Organizations, Possible duplicates. Search and filters (type, tag, has active matters, role). Table.

fields.name: roles_summary
fields.note: Example: 'client 2, adverse 1'.

fields.name: is_client
fields.note: Quick tab: clients | all contacts | companies | people.

fields.name: company
fields.note: For people: their organization.

fields.name: archived_tab
fields.note: Archived contacts with restore. Archiving is our delete: history and the conflict index stay. A true erasure (privacy request) leaves a name-only conflict stub.

actions.name: Create contact
actions.note: A duplicate check runs on save.

actions.name: Propose contact from email or document
actions.note: Created in 'proposed' state until it is used on a matter.

actions.name: Merge duplicates
actions.note: A merge rewrites conflict data, so a lawyer approves it. It is reversible for 30 days.

actions.name: Import contacts
actions.note: Opens contact-import.

actions.name: Bulk delete
actions.note: Admin plus lawyer; blocked for any contact on a matter, a bill, a trust entry, a note or a conflict record. Deleting instead archives and keeps the conflict index entry.

actions.name: Export vCard or CSV
actions.note: Audit-logged.

actions.name: Restore archived contact
actions.note: Restores the contact and its links; logged.

screens.agent: The agent finds likely duplicates by name similarity, email, phone and company registration number. It enriches organization records from public registries where the firm allows it, and proposes merges along with the reasons.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves every merge and every deletion, because both change what the conflict check sees.
edge: Two people genuinely share a name: the user marks them 'not a duplicate', which suppresses future proposals.
Deleting a contact who has matter history: blocked. Archive it instead.
A PIPEDA access request: export everything held on the contact.
Contact referenced by a closed matter: may be archived, never hard-deleted, so later conflict checks still find it.
Bulk delete selection mixes free and linked contacts: free ones archived, linked ones listed as refused.
screens.reg: Contacts feed conflict checks (RPC 3.4). PIPEDA applies to personal information. Prospective-client information is retained for conflicts even when the firm declines.

screens.name: Contact detail
screens.purpose: One person or organization: details, relationships, roles across matters, and ID status.
screens.layout: Header with name, type and ID-verification badge. Sections: Details, Relationships (graph and list), Roles on matters, Communications, Custom fields.

fields.name: aliases
fields.note: Former names, trade names. Used by the conflict check.

fields.name: date_of_birth
fields.note: Person only. Restricted field.

fields.name: occupation
fields.note: Person only. Part of the By-Law 7.1 identification record (verify).

fields.name: org_number
fields.note: Ontario corporation number or BN.

fields.name: relationships
fields.note: Examples: spouse, parent, director of, subsidiary of, employee of, member of firm.

fields.name: id_verification
fields.note: Status only on this screen. The documents sit in the ID area.

fields.name: type
fields.note: person | organization

fields.name: emails
fields.note: Each with type work | home | other and a primary flag.

fields.name: phones
fields.note: Each typed; primary flag.

fields.name: employees
fields.note: For organizations: people linked as staff, with title.

fields.name: custom_fields
fields.note: Firm-wide contact field sets, see contact-field-settings.

fields.name: portal_access
fields.note: none | invited | active; set from the client portal, shown here read-only.

fields.name: billing_defaults
fields.note: Client-specific rates per user or team, owned by billing. Precedence follows billing.json; Clio's documented order is entry custom rate > flat rate > matter rate > client rate > activity rate > user default.

fields.name: notes
fields.note: Contact-level notes.

fields.name: roles_across_matters
fields.note: Grouped as client of, party to, counsel on, other. Each row links the matter; walled matters count as 'restricted matter' with no name.

actions.name: Edit details
actions.note: A change to legal name or aliases re-runs conflict indexing.

actions.name: Propose relationship
actions.note: Example: 'director of Northgate Rentals Inc.', cited from a corporate profile.

actions.name: Request ID
actions.note: Sends a portal request. G4 applies afterwards.

actions.name: Open communications for this contact
actions.note: Calls, emails and messages not tied to a matter land here.

actions.name: Archive contact
actions.note: Same gate as delete (G-CM); contact stays in the conflict index.

screens.agent: The agent keeps aliases and relationships current from documents and public registries, citing each source. It warns when a new relationship links this contact to an adverse party on any open matter.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves agent-proposed relationships, because they change conflict results. Direct edits by staff are logged.
edge: Legal name change: keep the old name as an alias and re-run conflict matching across open matters.
Relationship creates a new conflict on an open matter: raise an alert to the responsible lawyer.
Someone without access opens a restricted field (DOB, ID): the value is masked.
Organization renamed (amalgamation): old name kept as alias so conflict search still hits it.
Person leaves an organization: employment end-dated, not removed.
screens.reg: BL7.1 identification fields (verify). RPC 3.4 related persons and entities. PIPEDA minimisation: collect only what is needed.

screens.name: Practice areas, custom fields and stages
screens.purpose: Defines, for each practice area, its custom field set, stage list, default task plan and conflict-relevant roles.
screens.layout: List of areas on the left. On the right, tabs: Fields (drag to reorder), Stages (ordered list with flags), Roles, Defaults. The agent's suggestions sit in a side panel.

fields.name: field_rules
fields.note: Per field: required yes/no, default-shown yes/no, picklist options, help text, 64-char name limit.

fields.name: field_type
fields.note: text | long text | number | money | date | time | picklist | yes/no | contact ref | matter ref | email | URL. Every Clio custom field type maps 1:1, including time of day, so a Clio import loses no field.

actions.name: Add or edit field
actions.note: An admin edits it and a lawyer approves before the change goes live. A field type cannot change once it holds data.

actions.name: Suggest starter set
actions.note: Ontario-flavoured defaults, e.g. Real estate: closing date, LRO no., PIN; Family: separation date, FRO no.; Estates: date of death, estate value (verify field names).

actions.name: Retire a field or picklist option
actions.note: Retired values stay on old matters, read-only; cannot be picked again.

actions.name: Make a field required
actions.note: Preview shows how many open matters would become non-compliant; they are flagged, not blocked.

screens.agent: The agent proposes a starter field set and stage list for each area. It spots fields that are never filled in, or free-text values that are always the same, and suggests turning those into enums.
screens.gate: A lawyer approves configuration changes before they go live, because required fields and stage flags change what the agent may do.
edge: Field deleted while it holds data: hide it and keep the data. Hard delete is not allowed.
A required field is added to an area with open matters: existing matters show it as missing, and nothing is blocked.
Stage renamed: history keeps the old label alongside the id.
Field made required while a bulk import is pending: import validates against the new rule and reports rows.
Renaming a field used in saved views, templates and document merge fields: references follow the field id, not the name.
Clio import brings a custom field type we do not support: the import dry run lists it and refuses that field rather than coercing it to text silently.

screens.name: Global search
screens.purpose: Search, or ask a question, across matters, contacts, documents, notes, emails and events, scoped by permission.
screens.layout: Command bar (keyboard shortcut) with typeahead grouped by type. The full results page has a type facet on the left and results on the right. An answer card at the top appears for questions.

fields.name: include_closed
fields.note: Default off for browsing, always on when run as a conflict check.

actions.name: Answer question with citations
actions.note: Uses only records the user can read.

actions.name: Run as conflict check
actions.note: Hands off to the conflict area. A search is not a recorded conflict check.

screens.agent: The agent turns natural-language questions (for example, 'which real estate closings next week still lack a title search') into structured queries plus a cited answer. It ranks results by recency and by the user's matters.
screens.gate: none
edge: A walled matter matches the query: it is excluded completely, including from counts.
Results include privileged documents: show the privilege badge.
Search used to fish for conflicts without a recorded check: point the user to the conflict check.
Search hit in a walled matter: excluded entirely, not counted in totals.
screens.reg: Ethical walls and confidentiality (RPC 3.3, verify). Search queries are audit-logged without storing their text in platform metadata.

screens.name: Matter templates
screens.purpose: Presets that fill a new matter: practice area, fields, billing, folders, team roles and the work template, with one firm default.
screens.layout: Left: template list grouped by practice area, default marked. Main: preset sections (details, fields, billing, folders, team, work plan). Right: 'used by N matters'.

fields.name: is_default
fields.note: One firm-wide default applied when the user picks none.

fields.name: description_pattern
fields.note: e.g. '{client} purchase of {property}'.

fields.name: preset_fields
fields.note: Custom field defaults.

fields.name: billing_preset
fields.note: Method, rate table ref, retainer floor; billing area validates.

fields.name: folder_structure

screens.agent: Weekly the agent ranks matters by access risk and proposes narrowing changes. It never proposes granting access to the admin who runs the report.

A walled matter is selected in a bulk change: it is skipped and listed; walls change only in conflicts.
A bulk widening is approved by some lawyers and declined by others: apply the approved ones and report the rest; never all-or-nothing silently.

fields.name: scope
fields.note: whole matter | documents only | emails only | a chosen folder | a date range

fields.name: answer
fields.note: Every sentence carries at least one citation to a document page and line, an email or a note. A sentence with no source is not shown.

fields.name: sources
fields.note: With preview; scans are searched through OCR text.

fields.name: history

actions.name: Ask
actions.note: Searches this matter only; walls and access apply to the sources used.

actions.name: Save answer as a note
actions.note: Saved as an agent-drafted note under G-NT; the citations come with it.

actions.name: Build a chronology from this answer
actions.note: Opens matter-chronology filtered to the question's topic.

actions.name: Report a wrong answer
actions.note: Feeds the harness evals with the question, answer and the right source.

screens.agent: Answers only from the matter's own record. It cites to page and line, says 'not in the file' when it cannot find support, and flags conflicts between sources (two different dates for one event) instead of choosing one.
screens.gate: Reading needs no approval. Saving an answer into the record passes G-NT; changing a key fact from an answer goes through G-KF.
edge: A source document is under a narrower restriction than the matter: it is not used, and the answer says one source was withheld.
Sources disagree: show both with citations and propose a key-fact check; never pick one silently.
A document is still being OCR'd: answer from what is ready and say which files were not searched.
screens.reg: Competence and supervision of technology (RPC 3.1 and 6.1, verify). Privilege stays inside the matter; nothing leaves the firm cell.

fields.name: event
fields.note: One line in the firm's own words.

fields.name: status
fields.note: proposed | checked | disputed. Only a person can mark a row checked.

fields.name: conflicts_with
fields.note: Another row or a key fact with a different date for the same event.

actions.name: Build chronology
actions.note: From the whole matter or a filter; rows arrive as proposed.

actions.name: Mark row checked or disputed
actions.note: Logged with the user and time.

actions.name: Add or edit a row

actions.name: Export to Word or PDF

screens.agent: Reads every document, email, scan and note in the matter, pulls dated events, de-duplicates them and cites each. It marks contradictions and links them to key facts so the lawyer can resolve them through G-KF.
screens.gate: No gate to build or export internally. A checked row that changes a key fact goes through G-KF.
edge: Two sources give different dates for one event: both rows kept and linked as disputed.
A source is deleted or restricted after the row was built: the row shows 'source withdrawn' and drops to proposed.
A very large matter: build in batches and show progress; never truncate silently.
screens.reg: Accuracy of the record (RPC 3.1, verify). Exports are work product and privileged.

open_questions: Can a matter open before the engagement letter is signed (an urgent limitation case), with a logged lawyer exception, or is G5 always a hard block?
Should matter numbering be global per firm (YYYY-NNNN) or per practice area? Do we keep legacy numbers on migration from Clio or PCLaw?
Should ethical walls hide a matter completely (404) or show a 'restricted' stub? The spec currently hides it.
Should practice-area starter sets (fields and stages) ship as product defaults per Ontario area, or does each firm build its own with agent help?
May the agent enrich organization contacts from public registries (the Ontario Business Registry) automatically, or only on request? This affects cost and PIPEDA.
Is a stage change by a clerk or paralegal into a non-flagged stage ungated, or do all stage changes need a lawyer?
Do notes and the activity timeline live entirely in the firm cell (yes per the brief), and what retention applies to agent activity entries after the matter closes?
Who counts as approver for G-NT when the call participant is a paralegal: the paralegal, or the supervising lawyer as well?
Pending status: does it mean 'not yet opened' or 'winding down'? Clio's own help and API disagree; we should pick one and add a separate 'closing' state if needed.
Should contact deletion ever be a true delete (PIPEDA erasure request) given conflict search needs the name? Proposal: redact to name-only conflict stub.
Do firms need groups (e.g. 'Family team') for access, or are per-matter teams enough for small firms?
Duplicate matter (could, r01): copy practice area, parties as proposals, fields and team into a new number with a 'duplicated from' link?
Stage board (could, r01): add a 'No stage' column with agent-proposed stages, and do we cap stages per area (Clio: 15)?
Stage history (could, r01): surface time spent in each stage per matter as a differentiator?
Matter overview layout (could, r01): firm default card order set by admin, per practice area, with per-user override?
Tags (could, r01): admins curate the shared list (Clio model) or anyone creates with agent dedupe; 30-day undo on tag delete?
Followers (could, r01): allow teams as followers, as Clio allows groups?
Contact permissions (could, r01): restrict a sensitive contact to named users or teams while conflict search still finds the name?
Personal targets (could, r01/r09): store annual target, working days and fiscal year end in user settings (time area)?
